the development of a new catalytic asymmetric synthesis of propylene carbonate.
the development of new synthetic methods for the preparation of chiral compounds, and the use of these chiral compounds as catalysts for asymmetric reactions.
the development of new catalytic processes for the asymmetric carbon dioxide fixation and asymmetric synthesis of chiral propylene carbonates.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymmetric carbon dioxide fixation into propylene carbonate was achieved by the reactions of optically active propene oxides.
the reaction of propylene carbonate with a chiral complex was found to be a good method for the asymmetric carbon dioxide fixation.
asymmetric carbon dioxide fixation was achieved by the reaction of a propylene epoxide with a bromide anion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chiral cobalt(III) complexes catalyze the cyclization of bromohydrin to propylene carbonate with high selectivity.
the asymmetric carbon dioxide fixation into chiral propylen carbonate can be achieved by the reactions of chiral bromohydrin with carbon dioxide.
the reaction is not only highly enantioselective but also highly efficient.
